stem:
The frequency distribution of daily wages (in Rs) of 40 workers is given below.

Class: 100-150, Frequency: 4
Class: 150-200, Frequency: 9
Class: 200-250, Frequency: 14
Class: 250-300, Frequency: 8
Class: 300-350, Frequency: 5

The modal class of the distribution is:

per_option_rationale.rationale: The class 200-250 has the highest frequency of 14, so it is the modal class.
Picking the second highest frequency class (9) instead of the highest (14).
Confusing modal class with the class just after the highest-frequency class, a common misread when scanning the table.
Mistakenly identifying the first class as the modal class without comparing all frequencies.

explanation: The modal class is the class with the highest frequency. Scanning the frequencies: 4, 9, 14, 8, 5 - the maximum is 14, which belongs to the class 200-250.

explanation_sections.punchline: Modal class = class with maximum frequency = 200-250 (frequency 14).
explanation_sections.approach: Identify the model: modal class in a grouped frequency distribution. Decisive move: scan all class frequencies and identify the maximum. Frequencies are 4, 9, 14, 8, 5. Maximum is 14 in class 200-250.
explanation_sections.lesson: The modal class is always the class with the highest frequency, not the class containing the arithmetic mean or median.
explanation_sections.timing: 15 seconds. Just find the largest frequency. Trap: do not confuse modal class with mode value; the question only asks for the class.
